Q.q: After a few weekends with no plans, I want to reach out to someone
Q.ex: On Sunday night after a whole weekend at home, I'm the one texting "Dinner next week?"

Q.q: When I start something new, I check the steps and how-to first
Q.ex: With a new appliance, I read the manual or watch a how-to video before using it

Q.q: When someone comes to me with a problem, I start thinking of solutions
Q.ex: While a friend vents, I'm already working out "What if you tried this?" in my head

Q.q: With a deadline, I tend to start early
Q.ex: If something's due Friday, I've started on it by Monday

Q.q: Even when I fail, I can move on fairly quickly
Q.ex: If I make a mistake at work, I don't carry it past that day

Q.ex: The day after a night out, I keep plans empty and stay home

Q.q: When I talk, the topic keeps branching out
Q.ex: We start on travel plans and somehow end up on where we want to live someday

Q.q: When someone comes to me with a problem, I take in their feelings first

Q.ex: When I hear "Today's plans are off," I get excited about what to do instead

Q.q: I often think back on conversations afterward
Q.ex: On the way home, I'm thinking "Was that the right way to say it?"

Q.q: Even at gatherings where I know few people, I start conversations
Q.ex: At a party with new faces, I'm the one asking the person next to me questions

Q.q: When I talk, I include concrete numbers and facts
Q.ex: I say "We waited 40 minutes" instead of "It was super crowded"

Q.q: For big choices, I go by the facts, not my mood
Q.ex: I pick an apartment by rent and distance to the station, not just a feeling

Q.ex: If it's Friday night and the weekend still has no plans, I get restless

Q.q: I don't really worry about what people think of me
Q.ex: If my posts get few reactions, it doesn't bother me much

Q.q: Before speaking, I sort out my thoughts in my head first
Q.ex: When asked for my opinion in a meeting, I want a moment to think

Q.q: I care about "what it all comes down to" before the details
Q.ex: During a long explanation, I want to sum it up: "So basically..."

Q.q: When deciding, I put people's feelings before being right
Q.ex: Even if a plan is efficient, I switch if someone really dislikes it

Q.q: I focus better when the deadline is close
Q.ex: Even with two weeks for a task, I get the most done in the last few days

Q.q: I easily notice changes in people's reactions or expressions
Q.ex: If a reply feels curt, I worry I've upset them

Q.q: My thoughts come together as I talk them through with someone
Q.ex: When I'm torn, my answer becomes clear while I'm talking to a friend

Q.q: When people tell me something, I want the details
Q.ex: When a friend talks about a trip, I want to know where they ate and what

Q.q: When we disagree, I explain my reasons rather than go along
Q.ex: If I'm not convinced by a plan, I say "That would cause trouble for X"

Q.q: I decide what to buy before going to a shop
Q.ex: I go in for "a white shirt" and leave with just that

Q.q: Once I decide, I don't think much about other options
Q.ex: Once I pick a shirt, I don't think about the other colors

Q.q: Deep talks with a few people are more fun than a big group
Q.ex: I'd pick a long chat with two or three people over a party of ten

Q.q: I often imagine "What if..."
Q.ex: On my commute, I think "What if I weren't in this job?"

Q.q: In a discussion, I notice who hasn't spoken
Q.ex: Even after a meeting reaches a decision, I ask the quiet person "What do you think?"

Q.q: For trips, I plan roughly and figure things out once I'm there
Q.ex: I book only the place to stay and decide where to go based on how I feel that day

Q.q: After choosing, other options still come to mind
Q.ex: After ordering, I see the next table's food and think "That looks good too"

Q.q: After seeing people, I have more energy
Q.ex: On the way home from three hours of talking, "I want to talk more" beats feeling tired

Q.q: I'm better at improving the current way than inventing a new one
Q.ex: Rather than rethinking from scratch, I cut the waste from the current steps

Q.q: If I'm praised, "reliable" makes me happier than "kind"
Q.ex: Hearing "You saved me. I knew I could count on you!" makes me feel most rewarded

Q.q: I finish one thing before moving on to the next
Q.ex: While I'm in the middle of a book, I don't open the next one

Q.q: Even with something new, I feel it'll work out somehow
Q.ex: When I'm handed a new kind of job, excitement wins over worry

Q.q: I reply to messages when it suits me rather than right away
Q.ex: Even when I see a message, I wait until I've settled down to reply

Q.q: I'd rather try a new way than stick to the usual one
Q.ex: Even though I have my usual route, I try a street I don't know

Q.q: When I team up with someone, I choose by personality over ability
Q.ex: I'd rather work with someone pleasant than someone who's just good at the job

Q.q: Working on several things at once suits me
Q.ex: I switch back and forth between three tasks depending on my mood

Q.q: Before something important, I go over my prep several times
Q.ex: The day before an interview, I check my outfit and the route more than once

Q.q: In group conversations, I find I'm the one doing the talking
Q.ex: In a group of five, I'm more often the talker than the listener

Q.q: When I learn something, I want the steps in order first
Q.ex: For a new app, I'd rather learn one action at a time than get the big picture

Q.q: When I hear someone's opinion, I first wonder whether it's correct
Q.ex: While a friend talks, I'm thinking, "Is that really true?"

Q.q: My packing for a trip is done by the day before
Q.ex: I almost never throw things into a bag on the morning I leave

Q.q: When I'm praised, I can simply accept it
Q.ex: When someone says "That's amazing," I can just say "Thank you"

Q.q: I'm fairly excited to go to gatherings full of people I don't know
Q.ex: I happily join events I'm invited to, even if I won't know anyone

Q.q: I start with the way that worked before
Q.ex: When planning a trip, I follow the route and booking method that went well last time

Q.q: When I tell someone something, what I say matters more than how
Q.ex: Even if they get a little annoyed, I say what needs to be said

Q.q: Even on days off, I decide the order of things first
Q.ex: I decide "laundry, then shopping, then cleaning in the evening" before heading out

Q.q: Even when I'm praised, I notice where I fell short
Q.ex: Even when told "That was great," I remember the parts that didn't go well

Q.q: Even at a fun gathering, I get tired first if it goes on long
Q.ex: Even at a lively dinner, after two hours I start wanting to head home

Q.q: When I hear someone's story, other ideas pop up right away
Q.ex: From a friend's story, I'm already thinking "Then you could also do X"

Q.q: When someone's in trouble, I help before taking care of my own things
Q.ex: Even when I'm busy, I find myself helping a coworker

Q.q: I move more easily when plans aren't too detailed
Q.ex: On days off, I decide what to do after I wake up

Q.q: I don't get very nervous speaking in front of people
Q.ex: Even when suddenly asked for my opinion, I can speak calmly

Q.q: I can spend a day off without talking to anyone and not miss it
Q.ex: After a whole day alone at home, I think, "That was a good day off"

Q.q: I'm drawn to things nobody has done yet
Q.ex: I'm more curious about what's coming next than what's popular now

Q.q: If I'm praised, "kind" makes me happier than "reliable"
Q.ex: Hearing "Thanks for always looking out for me" makes me feel most rewarded

Q.q: When I want to do something, I start before everything's ready
Q.ex: If I want to cook something, I start even if I'm short an ingredient

Q.q: My mood changes easily with what happens that day
Q.ex: On a good day I'm upbeat, and on a bad day I talk less
